newsitem.title: EAST TIMOR: Indonesia seeks guerrillas after East Timor ambush.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia seeks guerrillas after East Timor ambush.

text.p: Indonesian soldiers are searching for East Timorese guerrillas who killed a senior government official, an aide and four security guards in an ambush, military officials said on Thursday.
At least five people were wounded in the attack and in another ambush on Monday at a village near Viqueque town, 120 km (75 miles) south of Dili, the capital of East Timor, one official said.
"We have launched a search to capture them. Four platoons of troops have been deployed in Viqueque to find the rebels," one official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
"We believe there are 15 of them who conducted the attack, and their rifles include M-16s. The rebels stole the rifles from military posts," he said.
The military said the attackers belonged to the Fretilin guerrilla movement, which seeks East Timor's independence from Indonesia.
The official said Viqueque was calm on Thursday.
Residents and military officials said the dead were buried on Tuesday. "They were buried in the cemetery after a Catholic mass," said one resident.

The military has said one of the victims was Eugenio da Costa, head of the Viqueque regency's administrative affairs department. It said the others killed were another government official and four of da Costa's bodyguards.

The military said the attackers fired at a pickup truck da Costa was driving. The vehicle spun into a ditch and at least one of the victims died of stab wounds, indicating the rebels attacked the survivors, it said.
Two wounded occupants of the pickup truck survived, the military said.
Later the guerrillas ambushed another vehicle in the same area, wounding three employees of a company working on a development project.
The official Antara news agency quoted survivors as saying they could not recognise the attackers, who wore masks.
Military officials have said the number of armed rebels in East Timor is dwindling and do not number more than 200 poorly-equipped fighters.

Reported attacks by the rebels are rare. The Viqueque ambush comes more than one year after the killing of two people in Ermera regency, 65 km (40 miles) south of Dili. That attack was blamed on the guerrillas.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in an act not recognised by the United Nations, which still considers former colonial ruler Portugal as the administering power.
